# Character — Silent

**Character:** Silent

**Color:** Green

## Identity

The Silent is a nimble assassin who excels at Poison damage, Shiv attacks, and the unique Sly/discard mechanic. The Silent has the best defensive tools in the game (Footwork, Blur, After Image, Wraith Form) and multiple distinct ways to scale damage. The Silent rewards careful, patient play — setting up defenses while slowly poisoning or chipping enemies to death.

**Playstyle:** Defensive setup into scaling damage. The Silent wants to establish defensive buffs (Footwork, Blur, After Image) early, then kill enemies with Poison stacking, Shiv spam, or Sly-powered discard combos. The starting relic rewards building a deck with a strong opening turn.

### Strengths

- Best defensive scaling in the game — Footwork, After Image, Blur, Wraith Form
- Poison bypasses block and armor — deals damage regardless of enemy defenses
- Sly mechanic creates free card plays from discarding — unique action economy
- Excellent card draw and cycling — Acrobatics, Backflip, Adrenaline
- Shivs provide cheap, numerous attacks that scale with Strength and Accuracy

### Weaknesses

- Lower base damage than Ironclad — frontloaded damage can be lacking in Act 1
- Poison is slow — it takes multiple turns to kill tough enemies
- Shiv builds need specific support cards (Accuracy, Kunai, Shuriken) to scale properly
- Starting deck is weaker than Ironclad's — Strikes and Defends have lower base values
- Some strategies require multiple specific pieces to function well

## Starting Deck

### Strikes

**Count:** 5

**Damage:** 6

**Cost:** 1

**Note:** Remove as quickly as possible — Silent Strikes are the same as Ironclad's

### Defends

**Count:** 5

**Block:** 5

**Cost:** 1

**Note:** Remove after Strikes — slightly more Defends than Ironclad

### Neutralize

**Count:** 1

**Damage:** 3

**Cost:** 0

**Effect:** Apply 1 Weak (2 Weak upgraded)

**Note:** 0-cost with Weak application. Always play turn 1. Upgrade is high priority — 2 Weak is excellent.

### Survivor

**Count:** 1

**Damage:** 0

**Cost:** 1

**Effect:** Gain 8 block, discard 1 card

**Note:** Block + discard trigger. Excellent with Sly cards.

## Starting Relic

**Name:** Ring of the Snake

**Effect:** Draw 2 extra cards on turn 1 of each combat (7 card opening hand instead of 5)

**Strategic Value:** A larger opening hand means more options on turn 1. You can play more cards, see more of your deck, and set up faster. This rewards having strong opening plays and synergies.

### Tips

- Plan your turn 1 around having 7 cards — you can play more aggressively
- Innate cards are extra valuable with Ring of the Snake — guaranteed in a larger hand
- Discard effects on turn 1 are powerful — more cards in hand = more discard targets
- The extra draw means you see 7/20 cards on turn 1 (35% of a 20-card deck) — very consistent

## Archetypes

### Poison

Stack Poison on enemies to deal damage at the end of each turn. Poison ticks down by 1 each turn, so higher stacks deal more total damage. Catalyst doubles/triples Poison for burst damage.

#### Core Cards

- Deadly Poison — Apply 5/7 Poison. Simple, efficient, core Poison application.
- Noxious Fumes — Apply 2/3 Poison to ALL enemies at start of each turn. Passive Poison scaling that's always good.
- Catalyst — Double/Triple the enemy's Poison. The burst finisher — 20 Poison becomes 60 with upgraded Catalyst.
- Crippling Cloud — Apply 4 Poison + 2 Weak to ALL enemies. AOE Poison + defensive utility.
- Corpse Explosion — When an enemy dies, deal their max HP as damage to ALL enemies. AOE finisher.

#### Support Cards

- Poisoned Stab — 6/8 damage + apply 3/4 Poison. Attack + Poison in one card.
- Envenom — whenever you deal unblocked attack damage, apply 1 Poison. Turns all attacks into Poison sources.
- Bouncing Flask — Apply 3 Poison to random enemies 3/4 times. Multi-target Poison.
- Bane — 7/10 damage. If enemy is Poisoned, deal 7/10 damage again (double hit). Payoff for Poison.

#### Strengths

- Poison bypasses enemy block — it deals damage regardless of defenses
- Noxious Fumes provides passive scaling without needing to draw specific cards
- Catalyst provides enormous burst damage potential (20 -> 60 -> 180 Poison)
- Effective against high-block enemies and bosses with damage reduction
- Doesn't require much energy — Poison cards are mostly 1-cost

#### Weaknesses

- Slow — Poison takes multiple turns to kill enemies, especially in Act 1
- Weak against multiple enemies without Noxious Fumes or AOE Poison
- Catalyst is all-or-nothing — amazing with high Poison stacks, useless without them
- Enemy Artifact can prevent Poison application

### Shiv

Generate and play numerous Shiv cards (0-cost, 4 damage attacks) each turn. Scale Shiv damage with Accuracy (+damage per Shiv) and Strength. Play many attacks per turn for relic triggers (Kunai, Shuriken, etc.).

#### Core Cards

- Blade Dance — add 3/4 Shivs to your hand. The primary Shiv generator.
- Cloak and Dagger — gain 6/8 block, add 1/2 Shivs to hand. Block + Shivs in one card.
- Accuracy — Shivs deal +4/+6 damage. The primary Shiv scaling card.
- Infinite Blades — gain 1 Shiv at start of each turn. Passive Shiv generation.
- Storm of Steel — discard hand, gain 1 Shiv per card discarded. Massive Shiv burst.

#### Support Cards

- A Thousand Cuts — whenever you play a card, deal 1/2 damage to ALL enemies. Turns every Shiv into AOE chip damage.
- After Image — whenever you play a card, gain 1 block. Turns every Shiv into +1 block.
- Finisher — deal 6/8 damage per attack played this turn. Finisher after a Shiv-heavy turn.
- Choke — deal 3/5 damage whenever enemy receives a card (from Shivs entering play). Unique scaling.

#### Strengths

- Huge number of attacks per turn — triggers attack-count relics (Kunai, Shuriken, Fan)
- Shivs are 0-cost — they're free damage and free card plays
- Scales with Accuracy, Strength, AND attack-count synergies simultaneously
- After Image + many card plays = enormous block generation
- Can deal very high total damage per turn with enough Shiv generation

#### Weaknesses

- Shivs are individually weak (4 damage) without Accuracy or Strength
- Hand clogging — Shivs take up card slots in your hand, reducing options
- Accuracy is essential but not always offered — Shiv builds without Accuracy are weak
- Vulnerable to Time Eater (boss that punishes playing many cards per turn)
- Shivs exhaust after being played — they're one-use

#### Key Relic Synergies

- Kunai — play 3 attacks, gain +1 Dexterity. Shivs trigger this easily.
- Shuriken — play 3 attacks, gain +1 Strength. Makes Shivs hit harder.
- Fan — play 3 attacks, gain 4 block. Free block from Shiv plays.
- Ornamental Fan — same as Fan for some versions. Stacks with other attack-count relics.

### Sly Discard

Build around the Sly mechanic — cards that play themselves for free when discarded. Use discard effects (Acrobatics, Survivor, Gamble) to trigger Sly cards for massive action economy.

#### Core Cards

- Cards with Sly keyword — attacks and skills that trigger when discarded from hand
- Acrobatics — draw 3/4, discard 1. The best discard trigger — draw AND trigger Sly.
- Survivor — gain 8/11 block, discard 1. Block AND discard trigger.
- Calculated Gamble — discard hand, draw that many. Mass discard triggers all Sly cards.
- Tactician — discard to gain 1/2 energy. Energy generation from discarding.

#### Support Cards

- Reflex — cannot be played. When discarded, draw 2/3. Pure discard payoff.
- Sneaky Strike — 12/16 damage. Costs 0 if you discarded a card this turn. Free damage with discard.
- Concentrate — discard 3 cards, gain 2 energy. Mass discard with energy gain.
- Tools of the Trade — at start of turn, draw 1 and discard 1. Passive discard trigger every turn.

#### Strengths

- Free card plays — Sly cards don't cost energy when triggered, creating insane action economy
- Massive hand cycling — discard effects draw new cards while Sly cards play themselves
- Combines well with both Poison and Shiv strategies
- Very high ceiling — when the engine is running, you play 8+ cards per turn
- Deck thinning through discard cycling improves consistency

#### Weaknesses

- Requires both Sly cards AND discard effects — missing either half is bad
- Complex to pilot — sequencing matters enormously
- Can misfire if you don't draw Sly cards and discard effects together
- Calculated Gamble is risky — discarding your entire hand can backfire without Sly cards

## Act By Act Plan

### Act1

#### Priorities

- Upgrade Neutralize to apply 2 Weak — significant damage reduction from all enemies
- Find frontloaded damage (Backstab, Predator, Dash) to handle hallway fights
- Pick up Poison sources (Deadly Poison, Noxious Fumes) for scaling
- Get at least 1 good block card beyond Defends (Backflip, Leg Sweep, Dash)
- Remove 1-2 Strikes at shops

**Card Priorities:** Frontload damage > Poison/Scaling > Block cards > Card draw

**Elite Readiness:** Silent is slightly weaker in early Act 1 elites than Ironclad. Neutralize + Survivor help, but you may want an extra card or two before fighting elites.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure you have Poison scaling (Noxious Fumes, Deadly Poison) or enough attacks to deal with the boss over a long fight.

### Act2

#### Priorities

- Solidify your build direction — Poison, Shiv, or Sly/Discard
- Add key Powers (Footwork, Noxious Fumes, After Image, Accuracy)
- Improve card draw (Acrobatics, Backflip, Adrenaline)
- Remove remaining Strikes and Defends
- Upgrade scaling cards and key block cards

**Card Priorities:** Scaling (Poison/Shivs/Sly) > Block/Defense > Card Draw > Frontload

**Elite Readiness:** Your deck should handle elites if your strategy is coming together. Use Potions.

**Boss Preparation:** Wraith Form is the best boss card in the game — take it if offered. Ensure Poison or damage scaling is reliable.

### Act3

#### Priorities

- Skip most card rewards — your deck should be built
- Upgrade remaining key cards
- Remove any filler cards at shops
- Prepare specifically for the Act 3 boss
- If offered Wraith Form and you don't have it, strongly consider taking it

**Card Priorities:** Only take cards that directly address a specific weakness.

**Focus:** Optimization. Catalyst upgrade (double -> triple) is one of the most powerful upgrades in the game if you have Poison.

## Common Pitfalls

**Slow Act1:** Silent can struggle in Act 1 without frontloaded damage. Don't ignore attacks in favor of Poison — you need to kill things NOW in hallway fights.

**No Aoe:** Silent has limited AOE options. Without Noxious Fumes, Corpse Explosion, or Dagger Spray, multi-enemy fights are very dangerous.

**Shivs Without Accuracy:** Shiv builds without Accuracy or Strength are very weak. 4 damage per Shiv doesn't scale fast enough without buffs.

**Too Many Skills:** Silent decks can end up with too many skills and not enough attacks. You still need to deal damage.

**Wraith Form Without Plan:** Wraith Form gives Intangible but reduces Dexterity each turn. You need Artifact or a plan to end the fight before Dexterity loss kills your block.

**Catalyst Without Poison:** Catalyst is amazing but useless without Poison. Don't take Catalyst if you have no Poison application.

**Ignoring Footwork:** Footwork is one of the best cards in the game. +2/3 Dexterity permanently makes every block card significantly better. Don't skip it.

# Character — Defect

**Character:** Defect

**Color:** Blue

## Identity

The Defect is a broken robot that manipulates Orbs — Lightning for damage, Frost for block, Dark for burst damage, and Glass for utility. The Defect's core gameplay revolves around channeling orbs into orb slots, gaining passive effects each turn, and evoking orbs for powerful one-time effects. Focus is the universal orb scaling stat that makes all orbs stronger.

**Playstyle:** Setup-oriented engine builder. The Defect wants to establish Focus, fill orb slots, and let passive orb effects do the heavy lifting. Once the engine is running, the Defect generates enormous block and damage every turn without playing a single card. The Defect rewards patience and engine-building over raw aggression.

### Strengths

- Passive scaling through orbs — once set up, orbs generate block/damage without card plays
- Focus universally scales ALL orb effects — one stat powers your entire strategy
- Frost orbs provide the best sustained block generation in the game
- Dark orbs can deal enormous burst damage after charging up
- Creative AI and other powers can create a self-sustaining card generation engine

### Weaknesses

- Slow to start — needs Focus and orbs in play before generating real value
- Act 1 can be rough — starting Lightning orb provides minimal value without Focus
- Orb slot management is complex — channeling too many orbs can evoke useful ones prematurely
- Vulnerable when setup is disrupted (orb removal, debuffs targeting Focus)
- Many key cards are expensive (2-3 cost Powers) requiring energy management

## Starting Deck

### Strikes

**Count:** 4

**Damage:** 6

**Cost:** 1

**Note:** Remove ASAP — Defect has better damage options through orbs

### Defends

**Count:** 4

**Block:** 5

**Cost:** 1

**Note:** Remove after getting Frost orb generation

### Zap

**Count:** 1

**Cost:** 1

**Effect:** Channel 1 Lightning orb

**Note:** Basic orb generation. Upgrade to 0-cost is very good.

### Dualcast

**Count:** 1

**Cost:** 1

**Effect:** Evoke your rightmost orb twice

**Note:** Flexible evoke card. Good with Dark orbs for burst damage.

## Starting Relic

**Name:** Cracked Core

**Effect:** Channel 1 Lightning orb at the start of each combat

**Strategic Value:** Free Lightning orb means you always start with passive damage. With Focus, this becomes meaningful. In early fights, 3 passive damage per turn helps finish enemies.

### Tips

- The free Lightning orb means you start every fight with some passive damage
- Once you get Focus, Cracked Core's Lightning immediately deals more damage per turn
- In Act 1, the passive 3 damage adds up over 3-4 turn fights
- Consider Cracked Core when evaluating Focus — your first Focus point increases the Lightning's damage

## Archetypes

### Orb Spam

Fill all orb slots with orbs (primarily Frost and Lightning) and let passive effects do the work. Expand orb slots with Capacitor and channel orbs rapidly. With enough orbs and Focus, you generate massive passive block and damage every turn.

#### Core Cards

- Defragment — gain 1/2 Focus permanently. THE most important card for any orb strategy.
- Capacitor — gain 2/3 orb slots. More slots = more passive effects per turn.
- Glacier — gain 7/10 block, channel 2 Frost orbs. Block + Frost generation in one card.
- Coolheaded — gain 6/9 block, channel 1 Frost orb. Draw 1. Block + Frost + draw.
- Cold Snap — deal 6/9 damage, channel 1 Frost orb. Damage + Frost.

#### Support Cards

- Ball Lightning — 7/10 damage, channel 1 Lightning. Damage + orb.
- Barrage — deal 4 damage per orb channeled. Scales with number of orbs.
- Blizzard — deal 2 damage per Frost orb channeled this combat to ALL enemies. Frost counter AOE.
- Thunder Strike — deal 7 damage per Lightning channeled this combat. Lightning counter finisher.
- Reinforced Body — gain X*5 block (scales with energy). X-cost block card.
- Loop — evoke your rightmost orb at start of turn. Double passive effects from rightmost orb.

#### Strengths

- Enormous passive block/damage once set up — no card plays needed
- Focus scales ALL orbs simultaneously — one buff powers everything
- Very consistent once the engine is running — orbs produce value every turn
- Frost orbs + Focus can make you nearly invincible defensively
- Scales well into late game — more Focus = exponentially more value

#### Weaknesses

- Needs multiple pieces (Focus + Frost generation + orb slots) to function
- Slow setup — vulnerable in the first 2-3 turns before engine starts
- Orb slot management is tricky — channeling new orbs evokes old ones if full
- Biased Cognition's Focus loss can cripple the engine if not managed

#### Key Relic Synergies

- Inserter — gain 1 orb slot every 2 turns. Free orb slots over time.
- Data Disk — start combat with 1 Focus. Free scaling from turn 1.
- Gold-Plated Cables — rightmost orb's passive triggers an additional time. Double value from best orb.
- Emotion Chip — evoke orbs when you lose HP from an attack. Defensive evoke triggers.

### Focus Scaling

Maximize Focus as quickly as possible to make all orbs overwhelmingly powerful. Even a few orbs with 8+ Focus produce incredible passive effects. This is the 'quality over quantity' approach to orbs.

#### Core Cards

- Defragment — +1/2 Focus permanently. Always the highest priority card.
- Biased Cognition — gain 4/5 Focus, lose 1 Focus at end of each turn. Massive Focus burst with downside.
- Consume — remove 1 orb, gain 2/3 Focus. Trade quantity for quality.
- Core Surge — gain 11/15 block + gain 1 Artifact. Artifact blocks Biased Cog's downside!
- Equilibrium — gain 13/16 block, Retain your hand. Block + keep your hand for next turn.

#### Support Cards

- Recycle — exhaust a card, gain energy equal to its cost. Fuel for expensive plays.
- Self Repair — heal 7/10 HP at end of combat. Passive sustain.
- Machine Learning — draw 1 extra card per turn permanently. Passive card advantage.
- Echo Form — first card played each turn is played twice. Double your best card every turn.
- Buffer — prevent the next X instances of HP loss. Damage negation.

#### Strengths

- Extremely powerful once Focus is high — even basic orbs become devastating
- Biased Cognition + Artifact = 4 Focus with no downside
- Fewer orbs needed — Focus does the heavy lifting
- Flexible — works with any orb type combination
- Core Surge provides block AND Artifact in one card

#### Weaknesses

- Biased Cognition without Artifact is a ticking time bomb — Focus decreases every turn
- Needs to find Defragment and/or Biased Cognition — they're uncommon/rare
- Less resilient than Orb Spam — fewer orbs means less redundancy
- Consume removes orb slots permanently — can't undo it

#### Biased Cognition Management

Biased Cognition is the most powerful and most dangerous Focus card. Managing its downside is critical.

##### Strategies

- Artifact — each Artifact stack prevents one Focus loss tick. Core Surge gives Artifact.
- Orange Pellets — remove all debuffs by playing an attack, skill, and power in one turn.
- Win fast — if the fight ends before Focus drops to 0, the downside doesn't matter.
- Accept the loss — in some fights, 4 Focus for 4 turns is enough to win even with the decline.

### Creative Ai

Use Creative AI to generate random Power cards each turn, building an unstoppable engine of stacked Powers. Every Power you play makes the next turn stronger. This is a high-variance, high-ceiling strategy.

#### Core Cards

- Creative AI — generate 1 random Power card at start of each turn. The engine card.
- Echo Form — first card each turn is played twice. Double your Creative AI output or any Power.
- Heatsinks — draw 1 card whenever you play a Power. Powers replace themselves in hand.
- Machine Learning — draw 1 extra card per turn. More cards = more Power plays.
- Storm — whenever you play a Power, channel 1 Lightning. Powers generate orbs.

#### Support Cards

- Any Focus card — Focus generated by Creative AI or your deck improves your orbs
- Any block card — you need to survive while setting up the engine
- Hologram — return a card from discard to hand. Reuse key cards.
- Seek — search your draw pile for 1/2 cards. Find Creative AI or key pieces.

#### Strengths

- Highest ceiling of any strategy — unlimited Power generation
- Once running, generates incredible value every turn
- Each Power stacks with previous Powers — exponential growth
- Can pivot to any orb strategy based on Powers generated
- Heatsinks + Creative AI = draw a card every turn while getting free Powers

#### Weaknesses

- High variance — random Powers may not be what you need
- Very slow to set up — Creative AI costs 3 energy
- Vulnerable until the engine starts — no immediate defensive benefit
- Can generate useless Powers in specific matchups
- Punished hard by fights that get worse over time (enemy scaling)

## Orb Management Tips

Managing orb slots, channeling order, and evoke timing is a core Defect skill.

### Slot Management

- Default 3 orb slots — expand with Capacitor or relics when possible
- When all slots are full, channeling a new orb evokes the LEFTMOST orb
- Put orbs you want to keep (Frost for block, Dark for charging) in rightmost slots
- Put orbs you want to evoke soon (Lightning for immediate damage) in leftmost slots
- Plan your channel order to control which orbs get evoked when

### Frost Management

- Frost orbs are your primary defense — prioritize keeping them channeled
- Each Frost orb generates 2 + Focus block passively every turn
- 3 Frost orbs with 3 Focus = 15 block per turn automatically
- Don't evoke Frost orbs unnecessarily — their passive block is more valuable over time
- Glacier channels 2 Frost orbs and provides immediate block — excellent card

### Lightning Management

- Lightning deals 3 + Focus damage to a random enemy each turn
- Random targeting means Lightning is less reliable in multi-enemy fights
- Electrodynamics makes Lightning hit ALL enemies — transforms Lightning's value
- Lightning evoke deals 8 + Focus damage — useful burst when channeling new orbs forces evoke
- Multiple Lightning orbs provide sustained chip damage that adds up quickly

### Dark Management

- Dark orbs charge up (gain 6 + Focus stored damage) every turn
- Evoke Dark orbs when they've charged to high values for massive burst damage
- Dark targets the LOWEST HP enemy — useful for finishing off wounded enemies
- Let Dark orbs charge for 3-4 turns before evoking for best value
- Dualcast on a charged Dark orb deals enormous damage (evoke twice)

### Evoke Strategy

- Evoking is powerful but removes the orb — you lose passive effects
- Forced evokes (from channeling when full) should evoke your least valuable orb
- Plan channel order so forced evokes remove Lightning (damage burst) rather than Frost (sustained block)
- Dualcast is best on Dark orbs (huge burst) or Frost orbs (emergency block)

## Act By Act Plan

### Act1

#### Priorities

- Find orb-generating attacks (Ball Lightning, Cold Snap) for frontloaded damage + orb value
- Upgrade Zap to 0-cost — free Lightning channel every turn
- Get Defragment if possible — Focus ASAP makes everything better
- Pick up Frost orb generators (Coolheaded, Glacier) for defense
- Remove 1-2 Strikes at shops

**Card Priorities:** Orb-generating attacks > Focus (Defragment) > Frost block cards > Card draw

**Elite Readiness:** Defect can struggle against Act 1 elites without orb infrastructure. Having 2-3 orb cards and an upgrade helps.

**Boss Preparation:** You need some Focus or enough orbs to generate meaningful passive effects for the boss fight.

### Act2

#### Priorities

- Prioritize Focus cards (Defragment, Biased Cognition, Consume) above almost everything
- Expand orb slots with Capacitor if running Orb Spam
- Add Glacier for strong Frost generation + block
- Look for Core Surge if running Biased Cognition (Artifact prevents Focus loss)
- Remove remaining Strikes and Defends

**Card Priorities:** Focus scaling > Frost generation > Orb slot expansion > Card draw

**Elite Readiness:** With Focus online, your orbs should handle elites. Use potions to survive the setup turns.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure Frost orbs + Focus can generate enough passive block to survive the boss. 3+ Frost with 3+ Focus is very strong.

### Act3

#### Priorities

- Skip most card rewards
- Upgrade Focus cards and Frost generators
- Look for Echo Form if offered — doubles your best play every turn
- Remove any remaining filler
- Prepare for specific Act 3 boss mechanics

**Card Priorities:** Only take cards that dramatically improve your engine or cover a critical weakness.

**Focus:** Your engine should be built. Focus on upgrading and optimizing.

## Common Pitfalls

**No Focus:** Orbs without Focus are mediocre. 3 damage/2 block per orb is not enough to win fights. Focus is the highest priority card type for Defect.

**Too Many Lightning:** Lightning orbs deal damage but don't protect you. Balance Lightning with Frost for defense.

**Ignoring Frost:** Frost orbs are the Defect's primary defense. Without Frost, the Defect takes too much damage in tough fights.

**Biased Cog Without Answer:** Biased Cognition is amazing but the Focus loss will eventually kill you. Have Artifact, win fast, or accept the risk.

**Channeling Over Evokes:** Don't channel new orbs when your slots are full unless you want to evoke the leftmost orb. Accidental evokes can cost you valuable Frost or charged Dark orbs.

**Echo Form Sequencing:** Echo Form doubles the FIRST card played each turn. Make sure your first card is the one you want doubled — don't waste it on a Strike.

**Creative Ai Without Defense:** Creative AI costs 3 energy and generates value NEXT turn. You need to survive the turn you play it. Have block cards or potions ready.

**Orb Slot Starvation:** 3 orb slots is limiting. Capacitor or Inserter (relic) expands your slots and dramatically increases passive value.

# Character — Necrobinder

**Character:** Necrobinder

**Color:** Purple

## Identity

The Necrobinder is a dark summoner who fights alongside Osty, an undead companion. The Necrobinder manipulates death itself through Doom (instant kill thresholds), Souls (free cycling cards), and Osty (a companion that tanks and attacks). The Necrobinder's playstyle is uniquely strategic — managing Osty's HP as a secondary defensive resource while stacking Doom to execute enemies.

**Playstyle:** Companion-based strategy with death mechanics. The Necrobinder manages three unique resources: Osty (your living shield and attacker), Doom (a debuff that instantly kills enemies when their HP drops below the Doom threshold), and Souls (zero-cost draw-2 cards that exhaust after use). Mastering all three systems simultaneously is the key to Necrobinder success.

### Strengths

- Osty acts as a second health pool — enemies targeting Osty are not damaging you
- Doom bypasses the need to deal the last X damage to enemies — efficiency in combat
- Souls provide free card cycling that naturally thins your deck during combat
- Unique approach to damage — combining direct damage with Doom thresholds for efficient kills
- Strong exhaust synergies through Souls and other exhaust-on-use effects
- Osty can be resummoned — even when Osty dies, the Necrobinder can bring it back

### Weaknesses

- Osty management adds complexity — mismanaging Osty can leave you vulnerable
- Doom is a threshold check, not direct damage — enemies must also take regular damage
- Souls exhaust after one use per combat — your free cycling is finite
- Some enemies target you directly, bypassing Osty's tanking benefit
- Requires understanding multiple unique systems simultaneously
- Can struggle against enemies with very high HP that are hard to Doom efficiently

## Starting Mechanic

### Osty

Osty is automatically summoned at the start of every combat. Osty has its own HP pool, can take damage from enemies, and can be commanded to attack or use abilities through specific Necrobinder cards.

**Hp Pool:** Osty has a separate HP pool. Enemies may target Osty instead of you.

**Auto Summon:** Osty is summoned automatically at the start of each combat — no card or energy cost required.

**Death And Resummon:** If Osty dies during combat, certain cards and effects can resummon it. Some strategies even benefit from Osty dying and being resummoned.

## Core Mechanics

### Doom System

Doom is a debuff applied to enemies. When an enemy's current HP is less than or equal to their Doom value at the end of their turn, they are instantly killed. This means you don't need to deal ALL the damage — just enough to push their HP below the Doom threshold.

#### How To Use

- Apply Doom to enemies through Necrobinder cards
- Deal direct damage to reduce the enemy's HP toward the Doom threshold
- Once enemy HP <= Doom, they die at the end of their turn
- Doom + direct damage is more efficient than direct damage alone
- Example: Enemy has 50 HP. Apply 20 Doom. You only need to deal 31 damage instead of 50.

**Efficiency Calculation:** Doom effectively reduces enemy HP for the purpose of killing them. 20 Doom on a 50 HP enemy means you only need 31 damage to trigger the kill. This saves 19 damage worth of effort.

**Vs High Hp Enemies:** Against very high HP enemies, Doom requires significant investment. Sometimes direct damage is more efficient for enemies over 100 HP unless you can apply 40+ Doom.

**Vs Multi Enemies:** Spreading Doom across multiple enemies can be efficient in AOE encounters, but be careful not to spread too thin.

### Souls System

Souls are unique zero-cost skill cards. When played, they draw 2 cards and then exhaust. They exist in your deck at the start of combat and provide free cycling that naturally thins your deck.

#### Key Properties

- 0 energy cost — completely free to play
- Draw 2 cards when played
- Exhaust after being played — removed from combat deck
- Reset between combats — full Souls back at start of each fight
- Can be generated during combat through specific effects

#### Strategic Use

- Play Souls immediately for free cycling — there's almost never a reason to hold them
- Souls thin your deck as they exhaust, improving future draw quality
- Exhaust synergy cards trigger when Souls exhaust
- In long fights, generating additional Souls extends your cycling advantage
- Souls make your opening turns stronger — free draw 2 means seeing more of your deck immediately

### Osty Management

Managing Osty effectively is one of the most important skills for the Necrobinder. Osty serves as a tank, an attacker, and a strategic tool.

#### As Tank

- Enemies that target Osty deal damage to Osty instead of you — free HP preservation
- Monitor which enemies are targeting Osty vs targeting you each turn
- Healing or buffing Osty's HP extends its tanking capability
- A healthy Osty can absorb 2-3 turns of enemy attacks

#### As Attacker

- Specific cards command Osty to attack — these attacks don't cost YOUR attack cards
- Osty attacks can be enhanced through buffs and specific Necrobinder effects
- Osty's damage output is supplementary — don't rely on it as your primary damage source
- Some builds empower Osty's attacks significantly, making it a primary damage dealer

#### Death Management

- When Osty dies, you lose your tank — be prepared to block directly
- Some cards benefit from Osty dying (death triggers, resummon effects)
- Resummoning Osty mid-combat can reset its HP and provide a fresh tank
- Don't panic when Osty dies — adapt your strategy to play more defensively until resummon

## Archetypes

### Osty Builds

Focus on empowering Osty as both a powerful attacker and a durable tank. Buff Osty's damage and HP, and use Osty-centric cards to command it in combat.

#### Core Strategy

- Buff Osty's attack damage through Necrobinder-specific cards
- Increase Osty's HP or provide Osty-specific block to extend its tanking
- Use Osty attack commands frequently to generate free damage
- Resummon cards provide backup if Osty falls
- Balance Osty investment with personal defense

#### Key Cards

- Cards that command Osty to attack
- Cards that buff Osty's stats (damage, HP)
- Cards that heal or protect Osty
- Cards that resummon Osty after death
- Cards that trigger effects when Osty attacks or takes damage

#### Strengths

- Osty provides a second character's worth of attacks and HP
- Enemy attacks on Osty are attacks not hitting you
- Osty builds can have both strong offense AND defense through companion management
- Resummon mechanics make Osty builds resilient — Osty can come back from death

#### Weaknesses

- Requires Osty-specific cards — generic Necrobinder cards may not synergize
- If Osty dies and you can't resummon, you lose a significant portion of your strategy
- Some enemies bypass or ignore Osty, targeting you directly
- Investing heavily in Osty can leave your personal cards underdeveloped

### Doom Builds

Focus on applying massive Doom to enemies and combining it with direct damage to trigger instant kills efficiently. The Doom build is about efficiency — killing enemies with less total damage investment.

#### Core Strategy

- Stack Doom quickly through high-Doom-application cards
- Combine Doom with direct damage to push enemies below the kill threshold
- Calculate Doom efficiency: how much Doom vs how much direct damage is optimal
- Use Doom for efficient elite kills — save damage for the kill threshold push
- AOE Doom application can handle multi-enemy encounters efficiently

#### Key Cards

- Cards that apply large amounts of Doom
- Cards that apply Doom AND deal damage simultaneously
- Cards that scale Doom application over time
- Cards that apply Doom to multiple enemies
- Direct damage cards to complement Doom and push HP below threshold

#### Strengths

- Very efficient damage — Doom means you deal less total damage to kill enemies
- Strong against moderate-HP enemies where Doom threshold is easily reached
- Doom stacks persist — continued Doom application compounds over turns
- Can handle both single-target and multi-target with appropriate Doom cards

#### Weaknesses

- Doom alone doesn't kill — you still need direct damage to push HP below Doom
- Very high HP enemies (bosses) require enormous Doom investment
- Doom check is at END of enemy turn — enemies get one more action before dying
- Splitting focus between Doom and direct damage requires careful resource management

### Soul Builds

Focus on generating and using Souls for maximum cycling and exhaust synergy. Play many Souls per turn for free draw, then leverage exhaust triggers from their exhaust. Generate additional Souls during combat to sustain the engine.

#### Core Strategy

- Generate additional Souls during combat beyond starting Souls
- Use exhaust triggers (cards that benefit when cards exhaust) with Souls
- Cycle through your deck rapidly by playing Souls for free draw
- Thin your deck aggressively through Soul exhausts for consistent draws
- Pair with cards that benefit from high card throughput (many plays per turn)

#### Key Cards

- Cards that generate additional Souls during combat
- Cards that trigger effects when cards are exhausted
- Cards that benefit from drawing many cards per turn
- Cards that benefit from playing many cards per turn
- Direct damage and block cards to actually win while cycling

#### Strengths

- Massive card cycling — see your entire deck very quickly
- Natural deck thinning through exhaust
- Free card plays (0-cost Souls) enable playing many cards per turn
- Exhaust synergies generate value from every Soul played
- Extremely consistent once Soul generation is established

#### Weaknesses

- Souls are finite without generation effects — base Souls exhaust quickly
- Exhaust payoff cards are needed to capitalize on Soul exhaust
- Can deck out (run out of cards) in very long fights if not careful
- Requires specific cards to generate Souls mid-combat

## Card Tier List

### Tier S

Always take. Top-tier Necrobinder cards.

**Why:** High Doom application enables efficient kills against all enemy types


##### Osty empowerment cards

**Why:** Making Osty stronger provides free damage and extended tanking

**Why:** More Souls = more cycling = more consistency = more exhaust triggers


##### Key block cards

**Why:** Personal defense is still critical — Osty can't tank everything


##### Osty resummon cards

**Why:** Ensures Osty is always available as tank and attacker

### Tier C

#### Cards

##### Osty-death-trigger cards

**Why:** Situational — only useful when Osty dies, which you usually want to avoid


##### Niche utility cards

**Why:** Fill very specific gaps in rare situations


## Act By Act Plan

### Act1

#### Priorities

- Learn to manage Osty as a defensive resource — let it tank damage while you deal damage
- Find efficient Doom application cards to start killing enemies efficiently
- Play Souls immediately every combat for free cycling
- Pick up direct damage cards to complement Doom application
- Don't neglect personal block — Osty can't tank everything

**Card Priorities:** Doom application > Direct damage > Block cards > Soul generation

**Elite Readiness:** Osty gives the Necrobinder a natural advantage in early fights — use it. Osty tanking + your damage should handle Act 1 elites.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure you have enough combined damage (direct + Doom) to handle the boss. Osty will likely die in a boss fight — have personal block ready.

### Act2

#### Priorities

- Solidify your archetype — Osty-focused, Doom-focused, or Soul-focused
- Add scaling effects that compound over the act
- Improve Doom application efficiency for harder enemies
- Pick up Soul generation if going Soul builds
- Remove Strikes and Defends at shops

**Card Priorities:** Scaling (Doom or Osty buffs) > Soul generation > Block > Direct damage

**Elite Readiness:** Your strategy should be coming together. Use potions to cover gaps.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure your Doom + damage combo can handle high HP bosses within a reasonable number of turns.

### Act3

#### Priorities

- Skip most card rewards — your deck should be built
- Upgrade key Doom and Osty cards at campfires
- Remove any remaining filler
- Prepare for the specific Act 3 boss
- Ensure Osty resummon capability for long boss fights

**Card Priorities:** Only take cards that directly address a specific weakness for the final boss.

**Focus:** Optimization. Upgrade your highest-impact cards. Ensure consistency.

## Unique Tips

**Osty As Resource:** Think of Osty as a secondary HP pool. Enemies hitting Osty for 15 damage is 15 HP you didn't lose. This makes the Necrobinder effectively have more HP than other characters.

**Doom Math:** Always calculate Doom efficiency. If an enemy has 40 HP and you apply 15 Doom, you only need to deal 26 damage (not 40). That's a 35% damage reduction. Doom is most efficient on moderate-HP enemies.

**Souls Immediately:** There is almost never a reason to hold Souls in hand. Play them immediately for free draw 2. The only exception is if you have a specific card that triggers on discard and you want to discard the Soul instead.

**Osty Resummon Timing:** Don't resummon Osty if it would die immediately. Wait until enemies are about to attack (check intent) and resummon so Osty absorbs an attack.

**Doom Vs Direct Damage:** For enemies with less than 30 HP, direct damage is often more efficient than Doom application. Save Doom for enemies with 40+ HP where the threshold check saves significant effort.

**Soul Exhaust Synergy:** Every Soul that exhausts is a free exhaust trigger. If you have exhaust payoff cards (gain block on exhaust, draw on exhaust), Souls become even more powerful.

## Common Pitfalls

**Ignoring Osty:** Osty is not optional flavor — it's a core strategic resource. Players who ignore Osty management lose a significant defensive advantage.

**Doom Without Damage:** Doom alone doesn't kill enemies. You need to deal enough direct damage to push their HP below the Doom threshold. Don't stack Doom without also dealing damage.

**Hoarding Souls:** Play Souls immediately. Holding them in hand wastes their free draw benefit and clutters your hand.

**Osty Over Investment:** Don't invest so heavily in Osty that your personal cards are weak. If Osty dies in a boss fight (likely), your personal deck needs to finish the job.

**Forgetting Doom Timing:** Doom checks at the END of the enemy's turn, not the start. This means the enemy gets one more action before Doom kills them. Plan accordingly.

**Neglecting Personal Block:** Osty can't tank every attack. Some enemies always target you directly. Maintain personal block density.

# Character — Regent

**Character:** Regent

**Color:** Gold

## Identity

The Regent is a commanding royalty who wields two unique resources: Stars (a persistent secondary resource) and Forge (scaling damage for the Sovereign Blade). The Regent's playstyle is that of a strategist and commander — generating Stars to fuel powerful effects, building Forge stacks to make the Sovereign Blade devastatingly powerful, and managing dual resources for maximum efficiency.

**Playstyle:** Resource management and scaling. The Regent generates Stars through specific cards and abilities, then spends them to activate powerful effects. Simultaneously, Forge stacks accumulate to increase Sovereign Blade's damage. The Regent rewards careful resource planning — knowing when to generate Stars, when to spend them, and when to invest in Forge.

### Strengths

- Dual resource system provides flexible, adaptive gameplay
- Stars enable powerful effects that other characters can't access
- Forge + Sovereign Blade scales damage to very high levels in long fights
- Commander-style cards can buff allies or debuff enemies efficiently
- Resource generation + spending creates satisfying engine-building gameplay
- Stars and Forge both persist within combat, allowing for strategic planning across turns

### Weaknesses

- Dual resource management adds complexity — mismanaging either resource hurts performance
- Forge requires investment before Sovereign Blade becomes powerful
- Stars spent are Stars gone — misspending Stars on low-impact effects is costly
- Can be slow to start if Star generation and Forge building compete for card plays
- Some fights end before Forge/Star engines come fully online
- Balancing offense (Forge) and utility (Stars) requires experience

## Starting Mechanic

### Stars

Stars are the Regent's signature resource. Generated by specific cards and relics, Stars are a persistent secondary resource pool that persists across turns within a combat. Stars can be spent (consumed) to power up effects on other cards, or some effects may scale with the number of Stars you have without consuming them.

**Generation:** Stars are generated by playing specific Regent cards or triggering certain relics and effects.

**Persistence:** Stars persist across turns within a single combat but typically reset between combats.

**Spending:** Stars are consumed (spent) when playing cards that require Stars as an additional cost or that gain bonus effects by spending Stars.

**Scaling:** Some effects scale with the number of Stars you have, incentivizing Star accumulation before big spend turns.

### Forge And Sovereign Blade

Forge is a stacking counter that increases the damage of Sovereign Blade. Each point of Forge adds damage to Sovereign Blade attacks. The Regent's primary damage scaling comes from building Forge and swinging the Sovereign Blade.

**Forge Accumulation:** Forge stacks are gained through specific Regent cards and effects. Forge persists within combat.

**Sovereign Blade:** Sovereign Blade is the Regent's signature weapon. Its damage is directly proportional to Forge stacks. More Forge = more devastating Sovereign Blade hits.

**Scaling Curve:** Forge provides linear scaling — each point of Forge adds consistent damage. In long fights, Forge can reach very high values.

## Archetypes

### Star Engine

Focus on generating and spending Stars efficiently. Build a Star generation engine that produces Stars faster than you spend them, then use Star-powered effects for overwhelming advantage. The Star Engine archetype is about throughput — generate Stars and convert them into power.

#### Core Strategy

- Establish reliable Star generation early in each combat
- Build Star reserves before spending — have enough Stars to power multiple effects
- Identify high-impact Star spending effects in your deck
- Balance Star generation cards and Star spending cards (aim for ~60% generation, ~40% spending)
- Time your Star spending for maximum impact — save spending for critical turns

#### Key Cards

- Star generation cards — your engine's fuel source. Prioritize cards that generate Stars passively or as side effects
- High-impact Star spending cards — effects that use Stars for powerful outcomes
- Cards that generate Stars AND do something else (damage, block, draw) for efficiency
- Star-scaling cards that grow stronger with more Stars accumulated
- Cards that generate Stars at start of turn (passive generation)

#### Strengths

- Stars provide unique effects unavailable to other characters
- Star engine can generate overwhelming advantage in long fights
- Flexible — Stars can power offense, defense, or utility depending on the situation
- Some Star effects don't consume Stars, rewarding Star accumulation
- Passive Star generation (from Powers) provides value without card plays

#### Weaknesses

- Requires specific generation + spending cards — incomplete engine is weak
- Star generation takes card plays that could be spent on damage or block
- Spending Stars on the wrong effect is wasteful — recovery is slow
- Early combat can be weak while building Star reserves

#### Resource Management

**Generation Balance:** Aim for 3-4 Star generation sources in your deck. Too few and you starve, too many and you waste card slots.

**Spending Balance:** Aim for 2-3 high-impact Star spending effects. Too many and you won't have enough Stars to fuel them all.

**Timing:** Generate Stars in the first 2-3 turns. Spend Stars on turns 3-5 for maximum impact. Continue generating for sustained fights.

**Emergency Spending:** Sometimes spending Stars for emergency block is correct even if it's not 'optimal' — survival trumps efficiency.

### Forge Sovereign Blade

Focus on building Forge stacks to make Sovereign Blade incredibly powerful. This is the Regent's primary damage scaling archetype — invest in Forge early, then deal devastating damage with each Sovereign Blade swing.

#### Core Strategy

- Build Forge stacks as quickly as possible in the first 2-3 turns
- Play Sovereign Blade once Forge has reached a meaningful value (10+ Forge for good damage)
- Cards that build Forge AND do something else (block, draw) are premium picks
- In long fights, continue building Forge between Sovereign Blade swings for even more damage
- Upgrade Forge generation cards for faster scaling

#### Key Cards

- Forge generation cards — your primary way to increase Sovereign Blade damage
- Sovereign Blade — the damage payoff for Forge investment
- Cards that play Sovereign Blade multiple times or reduce its cost
- Cards that generate Forge as a side effect of other useful actions
- Cards that multiply or double Forge stacks

#### Strengths

- Very high damage ceiling — Forge has no cap, so Sovereign Blade can deal enormous damage
- Linear and predictable scaling — each Forge point is guaranteed value
- Sovereign Blade + high Forge can one-shot or two-shot even bosses
- Forge persists across turns — investment is never wasted within a combat
- Simple to understand and execute compared to some other strategies

#### Weaknesses

- Forge does nothing without Sovereign Blade — if you don't draw Sovereign Blade, Forge is wasted
- Forge investment takes turns that could be spent on damage or block
- No defense inherent in the archetype — must pair with block cards or Stars for survival
- Slow to start — Forge needs to reach meaningful values before Sovereign Blade is powerful
- Fights that end quickly (2-3 turns) don't give Forge enough time to build

#### Forge Targets

**Hallway Fights:** 10-15 Forge is usually enough. Sovereign Blade with 10 Forge should handle most hallway enemies.

**Elite Fights:** 20-30 Forge for strong Sovereign Blade hits. May need 2-3 Sovereign Blade plays.

**Boss Fights:** 40+ Forge for devastating Sovereign Blade damage. Build aggressively in the first 4-5 turns.

### Balanced Regent

Balance Stars and Forge usage for a versatile strategy that adapts to any situation. Use Stars for utility and defense while using Forge for damage. The balanced approach doesn't commit fully to either resource, giving flexibility at the cost of peak power.

#### Core Strategy

- Generate both Stars and Forge simultaneously where possible
- Use Stars primarily for defense and utility effects
- Use Forge primarily for Sovereign Blade damage scaling
- Adapt spending based on the specific fight — more defensive Stars against aggressive enemies, more Forge against tanky enemies
- Don't commit too heavily to one resource at the expense of the other

#### Strengths

- Most adaptable Regent build — can handle any situation
- Not dependent on any single card or combo
- Balanced resource generation means you always have options
- Can pivot to more offense or defense as the fight demands
- Easier to build — doesn't require specific rare cards to function

#### Weaknesses

- Lower ceiling than pure Star Engine or pure Forge builds
- Jack of all trades, master of none — may not have enough of either resource for peak effects
- Can feel unfocused without clear priorities
- Harder to evaluate card rewards — everything seems 'okay' but nothing is perfect

## Resource Balance Advice

Managing two resources (Stars and Forge) simultaneously is the core challenge of the Regent. Here's how to balance them.

### General Principles

- Generate resources you need FIRST, then spend them. Don't spend before you generate.
- In short fights (hallway), focus on one resource — usually Forge for damage or Stars for utility
- In long fights (elites, bosses), build both resources gradually over the first few turns
- Don't hoard resources forever — spending them is how you generate value
- Cards that generate BOTH Stars and Forge are premium picks — dual resource generation is extremely efficient

### Star Vs Forge Priority

#### Prioritize Forge

- Against enemies with high HP (you need damage scaling to kill them efficiently)
- When you have Sovereign Blade in hand or will draw it soon
- When your Star spending options are limited or low impact
- In fights where offense is more important than defense

#### Prioritize Stars

- Against aggressive enemies (you need Stars for defensive effects)
- When you have powerful Star spending cards in hand
- When Forge is already at a good level for Sovereign Blade
- In multi-enemy fights where Stars-based utility effects are more valuable

### Common Resource Mistakes

- Generating Stars without Star spending cards — wasted resource without a way to use it
- Building Forge without Sovereign Blade access — Forge is useless without its payoff card
- Spending all Stars early and having none for later turns — pace your spending
- Ignoring one resource entirely — both Stars and Forge provide value, don't neglect either
- Playing resource generation when you should be blocking or attacking — survival first

## Card Tier List

### Tier S

Always take. Top-tier Regent cards.

#### Cards

##### Key Star generation powers

**Why:** Passive Star generation every turn is the foundation of Star Engine builds


##### Forge multiplier cards

**Why:** Doubling or significantly boosting Forge makes Sovereign Blade devastatingly powerful


##### Sovereign Blade enhancers

**Why:** Cards that play Sovereign Blade multiple times or buff it specifically


##### Dual-resource generation cards

**Why:** Cards that generate both Stars AND Forge are incredibly efficient


##### Premium block cards

**Why:** The Regent needs strong block to survive while building resources


### Tier A

Almost always take. Very strong Regent cards.

#### Cards

##### Efficient Star spending cards

**Why:** High-impact Star consumption effects provide powerful utility


##### Forge generation cards

**Why:** Consistent Forge building speeds up Sovereign Blade's damage scaling


##### Star-scaling effects

**Why:** Effects that grow stronger with more Stars reward accumulation


##### Card draw and cycling

**Why:** Finding key pieces (Sovereign Blade, Star generators) consistently


##### Block + resource generation combos

**Why:** Block while building resources = efficient turns


### Tier B

Good cards for specific strategies.

#### Cards

##### Moderate Star generation

**Why:** Fills the engine but not as efficiently as top-tier generators


##### Direct damage cards

**Why:** Needed for hallway fights and as Sovereign Blade backup


##### Moderate block cards

**Why:** Fill block density requirements


##### Utility Star spending

**Why:** Useful but not as impactful as premium Star spending effects


### Tier C

Situational. Take only when specifically needed.

#### Cards

##### Low-impact Star generation

**Why:** Small Star gains may not be worth the card slot


##### Niche Forge cards

**Why:** Situational Forge effects that are only good in specific matchups


##### Expensive utility cards

**Why:** High cost for modest effects — usually better options available


## Act By Act Plan

### Act1

#### Priorities

- Understand which resource (Stars or Forge) your early cards support
- Find direct damage cards for hallway fights — Sovereign Blade needs Forge time you don't have in short fights
- Pick up Star generation to start building your resource engine
- Get block cards — the Regent needs defense while setting up resources
- Don't commit fully to Forge or Stars until you see what the game offers
- Upgrade key resource generation cards for faster engine startup

**Card Priorities:** Direct damage > Star generation > Block > Forge generation

**Elite Readiness:** The Regent can handle Act 1 elites if you have some direct damage and block. Don't rely solely on Forge scaling for Act 1 elites — fights may be too short.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure you have enough damage (Sovereign Blade + Forge, or direct damage) and block to handle a 6+ turn boss fight.

### Act2

#### Priorities

- Solidify your archetype — Star Engine, Forge/Sovereign Blade, or Balanced
- Add scaling that compounds over acts — Powers that generate resources passively
- Improve block density for Act 2's harder enemies
- Remove Strikes and Defends at shops
- Upgrade resource generation and Sovereign Blade

**Card Priorities:** Scaling (Star or Forge) > Block > Card draw > Direct damage

**Elite Readiness:** Your resource engine should be functional. Use potions to cover setup turns.

**Boss Preparation:** Ensure your scaling is online and can handle high-HP boss fights.

### Act3

#### Priorities

- Skip most card rewards — your deck is built
- Upgrade remaining key cards
- Remove filler at shops
- Prepare for the specific Act 3 boss
- Ensure your engine can start fast enough for the final boss

**Card Priorities:** Only take cards that directly address a critical weakness.

**Focus:** Optimization. Upgrade your most impactful cards. Ensure your engine starts reliably.

## Common Pitfalls

**Resource Starvation:** Not having enough Star generation sources means you can't fuel your Star-spending effects. Ensure you have 3-4 reliable Star generators.

**Forge Without Sovereign Blade:** Building Forge is pointless if you can't draw Sovereign Blade reliably. Ensure you have Sovereign Blade access (or cards that create/find it) before investing in Forge.

**Overspending Stars:** Don't spend all your Stars on turn 3 and have none left for turns 4-8. Pace your Star spending to maintain flexibility.

**Ignoring Defense:** Resource building takes turns. If you spend 3 turns generating Stars and Forge without blocking, you might be dead before the engine comes online.

**Slow Engine Start:** The Regent's engine needs 2-3 turns to start generating real value. Ensure you have enough block and early plays to survive the setup phase.

**Dual Resource Confusion:** Don't try to build both Stars AND Forge at maximum speed simultaneously — you don't have enough card plays. Choose one to prioritize each fight based on the matchup.

**Hallway Fight Overkill:** Don't build 30 Forge in a hallway fight against a 40 HP enemy. In short fights, play direct damage and finish quickly. Save the engine for elites and bosses.

**Sovereign Blade Timing:** Don't play Sovereign Blade with only 3 Forge. Wait until Forge is at a meaningful value (10+) for the Sovereign Blade to be worth the card play.

## Unique Tips

**Star Budgeting:** Think of Stars like a budget. Each turn, you 'earn' Stars from generation and 'spend' them on effects. Keep a positive balance until you're ready for a big spending turn.

**Forge Ramp Curve:** Forge builds linearly. If you gain 5 Forge per turn, by turn 4 you have 20 Forge. That's usually enough for a devastating Sovereign Blade. Plan your Forge ramp and know when to swing.

**Adaptive Resource Use:** In fights against aggressive enemies, spend Stars on defense. In fights against passive or tanky enemies, invest in Forge for faster kills. Adapt to each fight.

**Dual Generation Cards:** Cards that generate both Stars and Forge are the most efficient cards in the Regent's kit. They should always be high priority picks.

**Sovereign Blade Scaling:** Sovereign Blade is the Regent's version of Heavy Blade for Ironclad. It requires setup (Forge instead of Strength) but can deal comparable or higher damage.

**Star Spending Timing:** The best time to spend Stars is when you have a clear advantage — Star spending effects often provide burst power that ends fights or turns the tide.
